layer_at_fault_line: P3 is marked 'Fixed' for the authors merely stating their own view ('in our view'), not for declaring the part outside the test; file 33's line 'Fixed - the owner put this part outside the test, and said so' reads any owner-stated claim as fixed, though reporting.md's own caveat says a part 'the owner merely asserts... takes whatever mark holds it' and is never itself fixed.
quotes: P5 mark cell, two marks, excluded from marks_per_part: 'P5 fluid cognition | Borrowed / Loose | Schmeichel et al.; another account of the CET would serve as well.' -- P13 mark cell, two marks, excluded from marks_per_part: 'P13 continuum | Borrowed / Loose | Lishner's frame borrowed; the "divergent" placement is asserted, with no gauge.' -- pairs_that_pull excluded because a side is not a part label: 'Their own demand -- "valid, empirically evidenced tasks" -- pulls against P3, where the writing task is accepted as depleting without evidence.' and 'They also demand validation while conceding (P14) that no consensus on valid tasks exists; the standards they do give (clinical design, alpha) partly answer this.' -- test_swap (NAME ONLY) and test_rival (RAN) rest on: 'What separates them? The full-cross design (P12), or swapping in a task with a meta-analytic effect size (Dang). The authors name the first as future work but do not name a change that decides between "CET invalid" and "study truly null."' -- test_reverse (NAME ONLY) rests on: 'They run backwards from "no effect" to "the measure is bad." But some support (clinical design, low alpha, scoring bands) is independent of the result. Not a clean reversal.' -- turned_own_test (Y) rests on: 'Their own demand -- "valid, empirically evidenced tasks" -- pulls against P3, where the writing task is accepted as depleting without evidence.' -- question_identity and question_frozen_quote left null: the prompt supplies only the report's own frozen question, not the target line of the question as handed in, so SAME/MOVED cannot be told without guessing.
